- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk aversion or market panic.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to hold high forecasts; lower forecast by 3–6% for next period.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction within 1–2 periods.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/1.00 alternation, model exhibits oscillation bias — forecast should be smoothed with weighted average of recent 3–5 periods.
